html:
The Rape of Belgium is the name given to the German invasion of neutral Belgium in August 1914 and the killing of civilians that followed. It brought Britain into the First World War.

Germany's war plan was to attack France through Belgium, whose neutrality the powers had guaranteed in the Treaty of London. The German chancellor called that treaty a scrap of paper. Belgium refused to let the army pass, and Britain declared war. Belgian forts held up the German advance for days.

German troops, fearing snipers, shot about 6,500 civilians in the first weeks. At Leuven they burned the university library with its medieval books. Allied propaganda used the atrocities heavily. Most of the country stayed under occupation until 1918, with forced labour and hunger. The front line stuck near Ypres for four years. See Belgium.
sum: The Rape of Belgium is the name given to the German invasion of neutral Belgium in August 1914 and the killing of civilians that followed. It brought Britain into the First World War.
